title: Search, talk mode, two-camera sync, and much smarter selection
notes: Selection now ranks appeal, not just cleanliness — an on-device CLIP model judges whether a shot is actually good, blended with people in frame, motion, speech and stand-out sounds. Every kept clip explains itself; a skipped clip now names the specific rival that beat it, with the numbers side by side ("Why not this one?").

Reels rebuilt: a strict 60-second best-of cut with face-anchored portrait reframe, cut to music Meera generates herself with a known tempo, captions burned in. Karaoke captions light each word as it's spoken; every other caption ships as a switchable subtitle track plus a .srt file, not painted onto the picture.

Search your footage by describing a moment ("the bit where we're eating by the sea") and get timecodes back, built from the same analysis pass. Meera also names what's in the clip — dog, food, car and more — as filter chips.

Talk mode ranks a lecture, interview or wedding speech by what was said. Two cameras from one event are matched by what both microphones heard, correcting a wrong camera clock only on audio proof. Cuts now start and finish on a full sentence, not just the end.

Captions in your language: an optional multilingual model recognises Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Spanish, French and more, with translate-to-English. "Or just describe it" reads a plain-English brief into settings entirely offline.

Much faster: one decode pass per video shared across every model, machine-aware concurrency, and working GPU encoding. 4K export with an output-quality tier that never needlessly upscales 1080p footage. Installer trimmed by removing platform binaries that can't run on Windows.

Queue folders, watch a folder for new clips, save and reopen projects, resume a stopped job, undo and drag-to-reorder in review, and a restyled interface following Windows light/dark. A four-part review sweep fixed squashed Reels, a stabiliser that never stabilised, and several more real defects.
Five versions folded into one release since v0.2.0 — everything above is off by default unless noted, so existing behaviour is unchanged until you turn a feature on.

title: Smarter AI selection, portrait reframing, and a simpler screen
notes: Optional "Best quality" AI (CLIP) that judges whether a shot is actually good — sharper clip selection, smarter duplicate detection, and keeping the best of repeated takes.

Smart reframe for vertical and square exports: instead of blurred letterbox bars, it crops to the important area and fills the frame — and with the AI on, it detects people and keeps them from being cropped out.
Research-backed selection: keeps the most representative shot of each repeated scene, and can favour clips with a stand-out sound — a cheer, a splash, a laugh.
Optional finishing: colour-match footage from different cameras, cut wind noise, and a gentle Ken Burns zoom on scenic shots.

A much simpler screen — the default view drops from about 56 controls to the dozen that matter, with the rest one click away under "Show advanced" (and a bug that always showed the advanced controls is fixed).
Faster, sturdier rendering on long clips, with cleaner logs. Everything new is off by default, so your existing edits are unchanged until you turn a feature on.

title: Flags camera-clock problems that scramble a timeline
notes: Investigated clips appearing out of shooting order on a real 102-video folder. The ordering itself is correct — sorting by embedded recording time produced zero out-of-order clips, and for the 90 DJI files the filename and embedded times agree exactly.

The cause was bad data in the footage: 12 GoPro clips carried times contradicting their own file numbering (file 0501 dated Jun 21, 0505 and 0521 dated Jun 26, then 0526 back to Jun 21). That camera’s clock had been reset, stamping those clips four days before the rest of the trip so they sorted to the front.

A recording time that was never written cannot be recovered, so Meera Edits now splits footage on gaps over 12 hours and reports the groups — you can see immediately which camera is misdated instead of guessing why the timeline jumps.

title: Fixes a video disappearing from exports
notes: Fixes silent data loss. Full Journey Coverage adds back any source video the selector skipped, but a later cleanup pass could then delete that video’s only remaining segment — removing it from the export entirely, with nothing in the log to explain it. The cleanup now never removes a source’s last segment, and says so when it holds one back.

Audited every default that alters or discards footage, by measurement rather than assumption: sharpening/denoise is closer to the source than leaving it off (SSIM 0.9918 vs 0.9899), audio peaks at −12.8 dB with no clipping, and 8 genuinely distinct scenes produced no duplicate-skipping at all.
Upside-down correction remains off by default, as of 0.1.7.

title: Fixes videos exported upside down
notes: Fixes exports coming out upside down. Version 0.1.6 detected upside-down clips by assuming the sky is brighter and bluer at the top. On rafting footage — brown water high, a bright blue raft low — the raft was read as sky and correctly-shot video was flipped.

Automatic orientation correction is now off by default. Wrongly rotating good footage is worse than leaving one clip upside down, so it is opt-in via the new “Fix upside-down clips” option rather than something that can silently ruin an export.
With default settings no orientation changes are made to your footage at all. Everything else from 0.1.6 (repetitive-footage skipping, shooting-time order, sharper output) is unchanged.

title: Duplicate skipping and orientation actually work
notes: Repetitive footage is now actually skipped. Duplicate detection needs an AI fingerprint per video, but the AI pass only scored the top 25% of clips — so most videos fell back to a crude pixel comparison that could not tell one take of a rafting run from another. Every video now gets a fingerprint, and a video is described by the average of its clips instead of one noisy frame.

Upside-down detection rebuilt on a reliable signal. Comparing AI confidence upright vs flipped did not work — measured on real clips, an abstract shot with no true “up” scored higher than a genuinely upside-down one. It now uses a physical cue: outdoor footage is brighter and bluer at the top, where the sky is. Separation improved to roughly a 15x margin over ambiguous footage, and it needs no AI inference so it is much faster.
Indoor, night and abstract shots have no sky gradient and are deliberately left untouched rather than risking a wrong rotation.

title: Fixes freeze on large folders
notes: Fixes a freeze on large footage folders. The orientation check in 0.1.4 ran on every video up front with no progress shown, so a big shoot (170+ clips) looked stuck for minutes. It now runs only on the clips that make the final cut, after analysis, with live progress.
Includes everything from 0.1.4: true shooting-time order, repetitive-footage skipping, upside-down correction, and sharper output.

title: Correct ordering, fewer repeats, upside-down fix
notes: Correct shooting-time order across cameras — clips now also use the timestamp cameras put in the filename, which survives copying off a memory card (file dates do not, and used to scramble the timeline).
Skips repetitive footage — many near-identical videos (fifty takes of the same run) are grouped and only the best few are used, instead of grinding through every file.

Fixes upside-down footage — video shot with the camera the wrong way up carries no rotation metadata, so the built-in model detects it and flips it upright. Deliberately cautious: ambiguous shots are left untouched.
Sharper output — a light denoise and gentle sharpen pass on every rendered clip (Balanced and Quality modes).
Chronological by default — the auto-prepended highlights teaser is now opt-in, so a normal run stays in shooting order.

title: Smart scene dedup, music modes & overlays
notes: AI scene-similarity dedup — the same scene shot from a different angle is now recognised and de-duplicated using the neural network's embeddings, not just a pixel hash.
Background music modes — choose None, Smart (scenic parts) or Whole video.
World-class text overlays — five styles (minimal, elegant, bold, lower third, boxed) with font, colour, position and animation controls.
A run log is written next to your footage so any error is recorded even if the app crashes.
Keyless install, HEVC preview, overnight durability and correct icon all included.
